name: logisx
description: Dispatch and back-office platform for a trucking carrier (Node/Express + Google Sheets + Vue 3 SPA)

scripts.ci: npm run check && npm run test:unit && npm run build:client

//scripts: `npm run ci` is the exact gate CI runs — run it locally before pushing and the pipeline holds no surprises. `test:unit` runs the 45 standalone runners in scripts/ (~17 s, hermetic). It deliberately does NOT run test-suite.js: that one needs a live server, WRITES, defaults to port 3000 (production on the VPS) and with no SPREADSHEET_ID override writes to the LIVE Dispatch Management sheet. See the header of scripts/run-unit-tests.js.
//engines: A FLOOR, deliberately not a ceiling. Both the VPS environments now run Node 22.23.2 via pm2's `interpreter` (see ecosystem.config.js); the SYSTEM node on that box is still 20.20.1 and belongs to ~23 other clients' processes. 22.12 is puppeteer 25's hard floor — below it the PDF pipeline will not install. The exact version is pinned where it matters: `.nvmrc` and `node-version` in .github/workflows/ci.yml, so a green pipeline means 'passes on the runtime production actually uses'.
//overrides: Forces a patched uuid under googleapis. All four moderate advisories on this package trace to ONE root: uuid <11.1.1 (GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq, missing buffer bounds check in v3/v5/v6 when `buf` is provided). gaxios/googleapis/googleapis-common are each flagged only 'via' it. npm's advised fix is googleapis 128 -> 176, which is NOT taken deliberately: it pulls google-auth-library 10.5 -> gaxios 7, which moves to node-fetch v3 and implements `timeout` with AbortSignal.timeout(). Measured against a never-responding server: gaxios 6 retries a timeout (4 requests), gaxios 7 does NOT (1 request). That would silently convert every Google API timeout from 'retry 3x' into 'fail the user's page', which is the exact 150s dashboard hang the google.options() block in server.js exists to prevent. gaxios 6 uses uuid ONLY as v4() for a multipart boundary (gaxios.js:417), and uuid 11 still exports v4 for CommonJS, so this override is inert at runtime. Revisit only when googleapis ships a transport whose timeout is retryable.
